artboards.title: The row, and what a poll does to it

annotations.text:
WHO OPENS THIS
Farmers and miners, deciding who to sell a haul to. Not traders — nobody buys a share. A corporation's number is a signal about a BUYER, which is why the chip and the line matter more than the absolute value: what a player wants at a glance is who is climbing.

That is also the one place this departs from the iOS app it is shaped like: there, the order is yours to arrange. Here the list is five fixed corporations, so sorting by movement — best buyer at the top — may serve the actual reader better than the table's sort_order. Flagged, not assumed.

THE FIVE TICKERS ARE REAL
SFPD, HMMC, MUSE, EA and GOVT are the acronyms already in rp_corporations, listed in that table's own sort_order. The table even has a stock column waiting for a value — it reads 0 for all five today, so every number on these boards is SAMPLE.

IT NEVER CLOSES
So there is no Closed state, no pre-market, no previous close. The stats are windows instead of sessions — 24h high, 24h low, 24h open — and the header's live dot plus "updated 8s ago" is what tells you the number is current.

WHY NO LOGOS
The corporations all have badges, but a watchlist reads down a column of tickers, and a badge in front of each one breaks that column. The acronym is the identity here.

WORTH DECIDING
• What IS the value? rp_corporations.stock is an int. These boards read it as a plain index — no currency, no coin icon — because a share price you cannot buy would invite the question. If it is meant to be coins, say so and the rows pick up the purse icon.
• How often does it poll? "8s ago" on these boards is a placeholder for whatever cadence you want; the design only needs it to be shorter than a player's attention.
• Where does history come from? The ranges (1D through All) and the 24h stats need stored samples, not just the current int — that is a table of its own.
• Does a corporation's own page link to its employee list, or stay purely a number?
• Should the watchlist sort by movement rather than sort_order, given who is reading it?
